evidence.quote: Bitcoin Core Contributor Finds $0.35 Attack Could Link Bitcoin Addresses to Node IPs

Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail disclosed on Delving Bitcoin that a long-known privacy weakness in Bitcoin Core’s wallet rebroadcast mechanism could allow attackers to link Bitcoin addresses to the IP addresses of nodes tracking them for less than $0.35 per attempt. The method achieved a 100% success rate across 30 simulated attributions on a

regression test network (regtest), but has not been validated on mainnet. The weakness affects both hot and watch-only wallets, meaning an identified node does not necessarily control the associated funds. Other potentially affected software includes Bitcoin Knots, Sparrow in Bitcoin Core mode, Specter Desktop, Liana and Electrum Personal Server. Disabling

wallet broadcasting can mitigate the risk but requires users to broadcast their transactions manually. A proposed code change, PR #36482, remains unreleased and does not eliminate all rebroadcast-related privacy risks.
